note: Parkstad daily-life feeds. The tool rewrites air, power, maas, sky, roads, rail, notices and news; the run writes flu, noise, woord (Limburgs word of the day, appended), culture (dated local events, confirmed), admin (dated household admin), roda (next fixtures) and shops. Town-centre coordinates only; no address or postcode is stored. strikes: announced or threatened strikes and action days that touch daily life in Parkstad, the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany or French rail links, written by the run; the page shows the next ones and feeds them to the planner. protests: demonstrations announced or notified in the major Dutch, Belgian and NRW cities and in Maastricht, Heerlen, Liège and Aachen, written by the run; nearest first on the page.

flu.t: Week 44 (26 Oct – 1 Nov): 136 per 100,000 people saw a GP with a respiratory infection, a low level; RIVM on 4 Nov: few people with flu, no epidemic. Since September RIVM and Nivel report all acute respiratory infections, and the 2026–27 thresholds are not yet set, so the old 58 per 100,000 flu line no longer applies. Next update Wed 11 Nov.

woord.note: Heerlen spelling, as e-WLD records it for Heerlen and the gemeente uses it; Sittard and Maastricht write Vastelaovend. The example sentence is ours, since the dictionary gives forms, not sentences.

uitspraak.tip: oa is the long open o of English law; stress falls on LOA, and the final d is said as t

woord.note: Heerlens and Hoensbroeks alike: e-WLD records zauwele for both towns and the phrase ’t is an ’t zauwele for Heerlen. The noun is d'r zauwel, a drizzle, and Hoensbroek calls a light shower a zauwelbuuj.

uitspraak.tip: au as in English now; the -ele ending is two light schwa syllables and the stress stays on the first
